title: Fabrication Using Structural Steel Shapes
objective: Recognise common structural-steel shape concepts and the role of controlled drawings and identification.
safety_boundary: Recognition and drawing theory only; no cutting, forming, joining or handling procedures.

sections.heading: 1. Structural shapes
sections.body: Fabrication uses structural steel supplied in standard shape families and sizes for different design requirements.

sections.heading: 2. Identification
sections.body: Shape, size, grade and specification information must correspond with controlled job requirements.

sections.heading: 3. Drawings
sections.body: Drawings show how structural members relate to the intended component or assembly.

sections.heading: 4. Verify material
sections.body: Uncertain material identity or dimensions must be resolved before practical fabrication.

questions.question: Are structural shapes supplied in different families and sizes?
What shows how members relate in an assembly?
Should uncertain material identity be resolved first?
